notices.short_title: Gender Affirming Care
notices.description:
Pursuant to PPB Rule 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D), the NYC Health Department intends to process a Negotiated Acquisition solicitation as there is a compelling need for gender-affirming care services that cannot be met timely by competitive sealed proposals. NYC Health will contract with organizations providing or facilitating the provision of gender-affirming care to patients under age 18. This includes the prescription and administration of puberty-blockers and hormone replacement therapy to all minor patients for whom such services are medically necessary based on the prevailing standards of care. Services will be performed by qualified medical providers with current New York State licensure, and will be provided consistent with state laws governing parental consent. 

The proposed contract term for each contract is three (3) years, with a proposed start date of February 01, 2027 to June 30, 2029, with one three-year option to renew. The total estimated procurement value?is $8,879,218.00.

notices.plain: The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene intends to negotiate contracts with Callen-Lorde and Nonprofit Organization for Philanthropic Initiatives for gender-affirming care for patients under 18, estimated at $8,879,218 through June 30, 2029.

notices.short_title: NDA Healthy Families NAQ
notices.vendor_name: Crown Heights Jewish Community Council Inc
notices.description: The Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), as the designated Community Action Agency for New York City, administers the federal Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program to combat poverty and provide services that empower low-income individuals and families to achieve self-sufficiency. To maximize the impact of CSBG funding, DYCD targets funds to low-income neighborhoods designated as Neighborhood Development Areas (NDAs). The NDA Initiative promotes community-level engagement to ensure that services address the most pressing needs within each community. Programs use a strength-based approach, partnering with participants to build upon existing assets and capacities to achieve personal and community goals. Given the specialized nature of these services and the need for continuity and responsiveness to local community conditions, DYCD seeks approval to use the Negotiated Acquisition method in accordance with PPB Rule §3-04(b)(2)(i)(D). This approach allows the agency to negotiate directly with qualified community-based organizations (CBOs) that have demonstrated experience, trust, and engagement within their respective NDAs.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Crown Heights Jewish Community Council Inc. a $276,578 contract, negotiated with one vendor rather than open competition, for Healthy Families services in low-income neighborhoods.

notices.short_title: New York City Housing Authority Board Meeting
notices.description:
The next Board Meeting of the New York City Housing Authority is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 10:00 A.M. in the Ceremonial Room on the 5th Floor of 90 Church Street, New York, New York 10007 (unless otherwise noted). This Board Meeting will also be streamed live on NYCHA's YouTube Channel at https://www.youtube.com/c/nycha and NYCHA's Website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/board-meetings.page

These Board Meetings are open to the public. To provide comment in-person, all speakers are required to pre-register, at least forty-five (45) minutes before the scheduled Board Meeting. Comments are limited to the items on the Calendar. Speaking time will be limited to three (3) minutes. The public comment period will conclude upon all speakers being heard or at the expiration of thirty (30) minutes allotted for public comment, whichever occurs first. Comments may also be provided to the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by mail at 90 Church Street, 5th Floor, New York NY 10007.

notable.description:
The next Board Meeting of the New York City Housing Authority is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 10:00 A.M. in the Ceremonial Room on the 5th Floor of 90 Church Street, New York, New York 10007 (unless otherwise noted). This Board Meeting will also be streamed live on NYCHA's YouTube Channel at https://www.youtube.com/c/nycha and NYCHA's Website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/board-meetings.page

These Board Meetings are open to the public. To provide comment in-person, all speakers are required to pre-register, at least forty-five (45) minutes before the scheduled Board Meeting. Comments are limited to the items on the Calendar. Speaking time will be limited to three (3) minutes. The public comment period will conclude upon all speakers being heard or at the expiration of thirty (30) minutes allotted for public comment, whichever occurs first. Comments may also be provided to the Office of the Corporate Secretary by e-mail at corporate.secretary@nycha.nyc.gov or by mail at 90 Church Street, 5th Floor, New York NY 10007.

watching.short_title: InfoJini - Senior Data Analyst ETL - Alex Gak
watching.description: NYCERS had determined there is a need to hire a senior data analyst consultant with Extract, Transform, Load be responsible for detailed field level analysis, metadata analysis, profiling, and mapping of VSAM files into relational/dimensional SQL tables as well as conversion/validation efforts as part of an enterprisewide Legacy Replacement program; the senior data analyst will create and maintain the master data dictionary, and assist in database design of NYCERS mission-critical applications and inventory of its components.
watching.plain: The Employees' Retirement System awarded Infojini Inc. a $286,056 contract, through a small purchase, for a senior data analyst to map legacy data files into SQL tables and maintain a master data dictionary for its Legacy Replacement program.

watching.plain: The Employees' Retirement System awarded Rangam Consultants Inc. a $489,528 contract for a functional test lead to oversee user acceptance testing for its legacy system replacement and modernization work.
